Tell me one thing first if it matters: is this a technical case-screen (modeling, LBO, Excel test), a behavioral + fit loop, or a mix with senior bankers? I’ll start assuming it’s a 60–90 minute in-person/Zoom interview that combines behavioral fit and a short technical case (common for analyst finals). I’ll cover what to say, exact examples, technical checklist, and a 10-minute mock question to answer now.
What I’ll do now (assumptions stated): assume 60–90 minute final with behavioral + brief technical case; I’ll give:
- 6 behavioral stories tuned for an analyst role (one-line prompt, 2–3 sentence STAR answer you can say)
- A 6-step technical checklist and one short modeling/LBO script you can run through live
- 5 thoughtful questions to ask the panel (banking-specific)
- One mock interview question to answer now; I’ll score and fix it when you reply.

Behavioral stories — keep these tight, with numbers and what you did
(Use these as templates; replace [brackets] with your facts.)
1) Tell me about a time you managed a tight deadline.
- Situation: Last quarter we had [project] due in 48 hours after a scope change.
- Task: I was responsible for [financial deliverable / model].
- Action: I triaged tasks, reallocated work, ran a 2-hour modeling sprint, and stayed late to QC the outputs.
- Result: We delivered on time; the client accepted the deck with one revision and the team closed the engagement two days early, saving ~[X] hours of senior time.
2) A time you found and fixed an error in analysis.
- S: While preparing an industry comps table I spotted an outlier in EBITDA for [company].
- T: Confirm accuracy before the client meeting.
- A: Re-ran source spreadsheets, traced the error to a mis-linked cell, corrected the multiple, and recalculated sensitivity cases.
- R: The corrected valuation changed the recommendation and avoided a mispriced offer; senior associate praised the catch.
3) When you disagreed with a teammate or senior.
- S: Different view on valuation approach (DCF vs precedent).
- T: Persuade with data, not ego.
- A: Built both quick versions, showed sensitivity and assumptions, documented tradeoffs.
- R: Team used the blended approach I proposed; the committee approved and the client noted clearer assumptions.
4) Leadership/ownership as an analyst.
- S: Junior team short-staffed on an auction timeline.
- T: Keep the process on schedule.
- A: Took ownership of the CIM draft, coordinated with legal for redlines, and briefed partners daily.
- R: Process stayed on schedule; we advanced to Final Bids and I was given expanded modeling responsibility.
5) Fast learning / new skill.
- S: Needed VBA/advanced Excel to automate a recurring task.
- T: Deliver automation in one week.
- A: Self-taught key macros, implemented a template and trained two peers.
- R: Cut template prep time from 6 to 1.5 hours weekly; adoption across the team saved ~24 hours/month.
6) Ethics / handling confidential info.
- S: Received sensitive financials accidentally.
- T: Ensure compliance and proper use.
- A: Immediately told the PM, secured the files, followed firm privacy steps and logged the incident.
- R: No breach; firm updated process—praised for following protocol.
Technical checklist — what to have ready and how to answer
- Know the fundamentals: how to build a basic DCF (FCF, WACC, terminal method), three-statement linkages, and comparable multiples (EV/EBITDA, P/E).
- One-minute walk-through: be able to explain a DCF from revenue growth to terminal value in ~60–90 seconds, with the assumptions you’d test.
- Quick math: practice mental arithmetic, % changes, and leverage ratios (Net Debt / EBITDA).
- Excel tips to mention: how you check formula integrity (trace precedents, consolidate sheets, error checks).
- LBO basics: sources & uses, IRR drivers, debt paydown, exit multiple sensitivity.
- If they give numbers on the spot: state assumptions, round sensibly, show the path from revenue to cash.
Short on-the-spot LBO script (what to say/think in order)
1) Clarify the target: revenue, margin, purchase price (EV) or equity purchase price.
2) Build simple sources & uses: equity portion and debt tranches (senior, mezz).
3) Project 5 years: revenue growth, margin expansion, CapEx, working capital changes -> Free Cash Flow to Firm.
4) Debt schedule: interest, mandatory amortization, use cash to pay down.
5) Exit: assume an exit multiple on year-5 EBITDA -> exit EV; equity value = exit EV - net debt.
6) IRR calc intuition: highlight three levers — purchase price, operational improvement, and leverage. Walk sensitivities: +/-1 turn multiple, +/-200bps margin.
5 strong questions to ask the final panel (pick 2–3)
- How does the team win mandates in [sector]? What’s the most important skill for an analyst here?
- What deal or project from the past year best shows the firm’s approach to client work?
- How do analysts typically progress here over 24 months? Where do high-performers go?
- On a current live deal, what was the hardest modeling or execution challenge?
- How do senior bankers prefer analysts to present deck changes or urgent fixes?
Brief on tone and presence
- Speak precisely: “Here’s my assumption” before you state numbers.
- When you don’t know: say how you’d find the answer (check filings, run sensitivity).
- Use numbers and timelines; avoid vague phrases.
- For panel interviews: address the questioner first, then include others with eye contact (or camera nod).

Now the mock: answer this as you would in the room (type ~3–5 sentences):
“Walk me through a DCF.”

I’ll score it (structure, evidence, specificity) and give one concrete fix. One question: is there anything specific you expect they’ll test (modeling test, market fit, industry sector) so I can tailor examples?

You don't have any applications or an apply-queue on file yet. The one step that starts this is: pick a specific job posting for me to prepare an application for (paste its link here, or tell me the exact title + company). I will read that posting first and then prepare the exact submission card.

Below is exactly what I will put on the application card for the first posting, field by field, and where each value will come from or what I will ask if it's missing. I assumed a standard online application form for a company's careers site and that the employer may require a resume upload and some screening questions.
- Employer (company)
  - Source: the posting's company name.
  - Shown on the card exactly as the posting. You do not edit this on the card.

- Job title
  - Source: the posting's title.
  - Shown on the card exactly as the posting.

- Location / remote
  - Source: the posting's location field.
  - Shown exactly (city, state, or "Remote/Hybrid" as the posting lists).

- Job posting link
  - Source: the posting URL.
  - Shown on the card so you can open the employer page.
- Resume to attach
  - Source: the resume file or confirmed resume facts you have on file.
  - If you have no resume on file, the card will ask: "What name and email should go at the top of your resume?" (I will not guess). If you have multiple saved resume files or personas, the card will show which one will be attached.

- Cover letter / application note (if required or recommended)
  - Source: a short tailored cover note I draft from your confirmed facts and the posting text.
  - If I lack confirmed facts needed for tailoring, the draft will include [brackets] for missing items.
  - Length: about 120–250 words (kept concise to fit text boxes).
- Screening questions (Yes/No or short answers)
  - Examples: "Are you authorized to work in [country]?", "Will you now or in the future require sponsorship?", "Do you have X years' experience?", "Salary expectation?", "Earliest start date?"
  - Source: your confirmed profile facts when present.
  - If a required screening question is missing from your confirmed facts, the card will show a proposed answer using a sensible default and flag it so you can change it. I will never answer sponsorship or authorization questions without your confirmed facts.
- Work history / employment entries (if the form asks to paste full jobs)
  - Source: your confirmed facts or resume PDF.
  - If the job form requires manual entries and you haven't confirmed those facts, fields will show [brackets] for employer, title, dates and responsibilities and the card will ask you to confirm or fill them.

- Education
  - Source: confirmed facts or resume.
  - If missing, shown as [brackets] and left for you to confirm.
- Attachments
  - Resume PDF (explicitly named on the card) — I will state which file will be attached.
  - Cover letter PDF (optional) — I will state whether I will attach one.
  - Other documents (certifications, portfolio links, transcripts) — listed if the posting requests them; otherwise noted as not provided.

- Portfolio / work samples / links
  - Source: links you have confirmed in your profile or that you paste in this chat.
  - If the posting asks for links and none are confirmed, the card flags it.
- Salary field
  - If the posting lists pay, that value is shown.
  - If the posting asks for expected salary and the posting doesn't list pay, the card will show a suggested answer only if you have pay data confirmed on file; otherwise it will leave it for you to enter. I do not invent market pay.

- Equal opportunity / voluntary self-ID questions
  - I will not fill these in the card unless you tell me how to answer; they remain for you to complete.

- Referral / source
  - If the posting asks "who referred you," I will leave it blank unless you specify someone.
- Job-specific fields (e.g., GitHub, LinkedIn, coding challenge links)
  - Source: fields you provided or confirmed facts.
  - If required and missing, the card will flag them.

- Consent, signature, and checkbox confirmations
  - I will not check or sign these for you in the card; they will be shown as required items you must approve on the employer form when submitting.

- Internal tailoring note (for you)
  - I will add a 1–3 line note explaining what I tailored: which top skills/keywords from the posting I emphasized and any gaps (for example: "Emphasized X and Y; posting asks for Z which is unconfirmed").
- Final checklist shown on the card
  - Attachments included (yes/no and file names).
  - Screening questions filled (flagged if any defaults used).
  - Required documents present (flag if missing).
  - Items you must edit before submitting (EEO, signature, one-time codes).

What I will not do automatically
- I will not submit the application. Nothing is sent until you review and approve the application card in your extension.
- I will not invent or confirm facts about your work authorization, pay history, education or employment; any missing facts will be shown as [brackets] and must be filled or confirmed by you.
- I will not check boxes that require your consent or one-time codes.
Next step: paste the posting link here (or tell me the exact title + company) and I will read it and prepare the first application card with the fields above filled in from the posting and your confirmed profile facts. Is that the posting you want me to use?
